verdicts.reasons: The only real difference between A and B is how they mark the terms. A puts a filled amber 'Proposed' pill on every row (default, route-grant, approved-narrowed, long-content). B says it once with a 'Proposed by the agent' label above the rows. In A, the five amber pills pull the eye away from the amber 'Needs approval' status and the RIVER-48 binding code. They repeat one word five times and use a filled badge style that Kantel's session list doesn't use, since it shows status as a dot and text. At 420px (default-420 and mobile-420) the pill column takes width, so A wraps 'Authorization: Bearer {{secret}}' onto two lines while B fits it on one. In long-content, A's narrower value column also wraps the Path and Injection values more. Both versions share the same weaknesses. The expired story is pixel-identical. Button labels such as 'Open in vault' sit slightly off-centre at 1280. The approved-narrowed story shows '720h left' instead of a readable duration. The long-content approved row wraps awkwardly into a narrow column.

The one real difference is how the terms table is marked. A puts an amber 'Proposed' pill on every row (Host, Methods, Path, Injection, Lifetime). B says 'Proposed by the agent' once above the rows. In A's default, route-grant and approved-narrowed stories, those five amber pills fight the amber 'Needs approval' badge and the RIVER-48 binding code for attention. They also repeat one fact five times and use a filled-chip style, while Kantel's session list shows status as a dot and text. The pill column also takes width from the values. In A's 420px default and mobile shots, 'Authorization: Bearer {{secret}}' wraps onto two lines but fits on one line in B. In the long-content story, A's path and injection values wrap more tightly than B's. The expired story is pixel-identical in both. Both versions share the same remaining issues: a blue primary button next to the amber status, a progress bar plus '14:59 left' that repeats the 'Lifetime 15 minutes left' row, and an extra footer line. Those cap fidelity and cost for both.

The only visible difference is how the terms are marked as proposed. A puts a filled amber 'Proposed' chip on every term row (five per card in default, route-grant and approved-narrowed), and B has one quiet 'Proposed by the agent' label above the list. In A, ten-plus amber pills compete with the amber 'Needs approval' status and pull the eye away from the RIVER-48 binding code, which the card says is the one thing to check. B keeps amber for the status and the card border only, which matches the session list's restrained dot-and-text status style. In A the chip column also takes width: in default-420 and mobile-420 'Authorization: Bearer {{secret}}' wraps onto two lines, while B keeps it on one. In long-content, B's path and injection values wrap less. Both share the same remaining weaknesses: lifetime is shown twice ('15 minutes left' and '14:59 left'), approved-narrowed shows '720h left', and the expired and approved rows are identical.
